topics.topic_name: Raspberry Pi SBC Architecture & Hardware Setup
topics.description: Raspberry Pi platform, raspi-config, Linux OS, and GPIO modes.

questions.question: Which popular single-board computer (SBC) is used in Week 7 for implementing IoT remote data logging?
questions.justification: Raspberry Pi is a compact single-board computer widely used for hardware IoT experiments.

questions.question: Which tool/command expands the Raspberry Pi filesystem to cover the entire SD card storage after a fresh installation (Week 6 Assignment Question 7)?
questions.justification: The 'sudo raspi-config' utility menu provides the option to expand the root filesystem over the SD card.

questions.question: What operating system is standard on Raspberry Pi for running Python IoT scripts?
questions.justification: Raspberry Pi OS (formerly Raspbian), a Debian-based Linux distribution, is the standard OS.

questions.question: What does GPIO stand for on single-board computers like the Raspberry Pi?
questions.justification: GPIO pins are General Purpose Input Output header pins used to interface sensors and actuators.

questions.question: Which command captures a camera image from the terminal on a Raspberry Pi as tested in Week 6 Assignment Question 11?
questions.justification: The 'raspistill -o image_name.jpg' command triggers the Raspberry Pi camera module from terminal.

questions.question: In Python GPIO programming on Raspberry Pi, what is the purpose of GPIO.setmode(GPIO.BOARD) as evaluated in Week 6 Question 12?

options.A: To specify that pin numbering will follow the physical board pin numbers rather than Broadcom BCM channel numbers
options.B: To set all pins to 5V output

questions.justification: GPIO.BOARD configures pin references based on physical pin header numbers (1 to 40).

questions.question: Contrast GPIO.BOARD and GPIO.BCM pin numbering modes on a Raspberry Pi.

options.A: GPIO.BOARD refers to physical pin header locations; GPIO.BCM refers to lower-level Broadcom SoC channel numbers
options.B: GPIO.BCM is for analog signals; BOARD is for digital
options.C: GPIO.BOARD is deprecated; BCM is for AC mains
options.D: They are identical in every way

questions.justification: GPIO.BOARD uses physical pin header layout numbers; GPIO.BCM uses Broadcom SoC GPIO channel assignments.

questions.question: Why is GPIO.setwarnings(False) often included at the beginning of Raspberry Pi GPIO scripts?

options.A: To suppress runtime warnings when re-configuring pins that were already set in previous script executions

questions.justification: GPIO.setwarnings(False) prevents GPIO library warning messages when reusing pins without prior cleanup.

questions.question: What function should be called at the end of a Raspberry Pi GPIO script to safely reset pin modes?
questions.justification: GPIO.cleanup() releases GPIO resources and resets pin configurations to safe default states.

questions.question: Which hardware components are required for the basic DHT22 temperature logging setup on Raspberry Pi (Week 7 slides)?

options.A: Raspberry Pi, DHT22 sensor, 4.7K ohm pull-up resistor, breadboard, and jumper wires

questions.justification: The remote logging setup requires a Raspberry Pi, DHT sensor, 4.7k resistor, jumper wires, and breadboard.

topics.description: DHT22 pinout, 3.3V/GND/Data wiring, pull-up resistors, and single-wire timing.

questions.question: How many physical pins are present on a standard DHT22 sensor module (from left to right)?

options.A: 4 pins (PIN 1: VCC, PIN 2: Data, PIN 3: Null, PIN 4: GND)

questions.justification: The DHT22 package has 4 pins: Pin 1 (VCC), Pin 2 (Data), Pin 3 (Null/NC), and Pin 4 (GND).

questions.question: In the Week 7 Raspberry Pi-DHT sensor wiring diagram, to which voltage pin on the Pi is Pin 1 (VCC) connected?
questions.justification: Pin 1 (VCC) of the DHT sensor connects to the 3.3V (or 5V) power rail on the Raspberry Pi.

questions.question: In the Week 7 wiring setup, to which pin on the Raspberry Pi is Pin 4 (GND) of the DHT sensor connected?
questions.justification: Pin 4 of the DHT sensor connects to a Ground (GND) pin on the Raspberry Pi.

questions.question: Which pin on the DHT sensor outputs digital environmental readings to the Raspberry Pi GPIO input pin?
questions.justification: Pin 2 is the data line carrying digitized humidity and temperature signals.

questions.question: What resistor value is connected between Pin 1 (VCC) and Pin 2 (Data) of the DHT sensor as a pull-up resistor in the Week 7 slides?
questions.justification: A 4.7K ohm pull-up resistor is placed between VCC and Data to stabilize signal transitions.

questions.question: What type of signal communication protocol does the DHT22 sensor use to transmit data to the microcontroller?

options.A: Custom single-wire bi-directional digital serial protocol with timing pulses

questions.justification: DHT sensors use a proprietary single-wire time-critical pulse protocol.

questions.question: In the Week 7 sensor-Pi interface script, if physical Pin 11 (GPIO 17 in BCM mode) is connected to DHT Pin 2, how does Adafruit library identify the pin when using BCM mode?
questions.justification: The Adafruit_DHT library natively expects Broadcom (BCM) GPIO pin numbering (e.g., GPIO 17).

questions.question: What physical property causes the capacitive humidity element inside a DHT sensor to change output digital values?

options.A: Changes in relative humidity alter the dielectric constant of the moisture-absorbing polymer film

questions.justification: Relative humidity changes the capacitance across a moisture-sensitive substrate in the sensor.

questions.question: Why is Pin 3 on a standard 4-pin DHT22 sensor left unconnected (Null)?

options.A: Pin 3 is an unused dummy pin introduced for mechanical package stability
options.B: Pin 3 is for high-voltage AC input
options.D: Pin 3 is an optical fiber input

questions.justification: Pin 3 has no internal electrical connection; it exists purely for mechanical pin header alignment.

questions.question: What is the typical sampling frequency limit for reading a DHT22 sensor reliably?
questions.justification: DHT22 requires a ~2-second delay between consecutive readings to prevent self-heating and data corruption.

topics.topic_name: Python Software Libraries & Remote Data Logging
topics.description: Adafruit_DHT library, read_retry(), socket transmission, and relay control.

questions.question: Which Python library is specifically downloaded and installed to interface the DHT sensor on Raspberry Pi (Week 6 Assignment Question 13/14)?
questions.justification: The Adafruit_Python_DHT library provides functions to read DHT sensors.

questions.question: Which command is used to install the cloned Adafruit DHT library in Raspberry Pi terminal (Week 6 Question 13)?
questions.justification: 'sudo python setup.py install' compiles and installs the downloaded library package.

questions.question: Which Adafruit library function reads data from the sensor with automatic retry attempts upon timing errors (Week 7 slides)?
questions.justification: Adafruit_DHT.read_retry() attempts multiple reads until a valid checksum packet is received.

questions.question: In the Python script IOTSR.py, what variables store the returned values from Adafruit_DHT.read_retry()?
questions.justification: The function returns a tuple (humidity, temperature).

questions.question: In the client-server socket logging setup shown in Week 7, how is sensor data transmitted from the Pi to a central server?
questions.justification: Data is transmitted over network sockets using client-server socket programming.

questions.question: Why is Adafruit_DHT.read_retry() preferred over Adafruit_DHT.read() in Python scripts?

options.A: Single-wire timing pulses on non-real-time Linux OS can fail; read_retry() automatically retries up to 15 times to ensure valid readings

questions.justification: Linux is not a real-time OS; microsecond timing glitches occur, making automatic retry essential for reliable readings.

questions.question: In socket programming for IoT data logging, what happens if the server port number specified in client code does not match the listening port on the server (Week 6 Question 4)?

options.A: The client connection is refused, and data transmission fails
options.C: The server automatically changes its port

questions.justification: Client and server must use matching port numbers; mismatched ports result in connection failure.

questions.question: How does a remote server handle incoming sensor data streams in the Week 7 logging architecture?

options.A: The server accepts socket connections, receives text formatted data, appends it to a log file, and plots real-time trends using Matplotlib
options.B: The server converts data to analog radio
options.C: The server immediately deletes incoming files

questions.justification: The server logs received sensor payloads into text/CSV files and can plot trend curves.

questions.question: In the Python script formatting line `print('Temp={0:0.1f}*C humidity={1:0.1f}%'.format(temperature, humidity))`, what does `{0:0.1f}` specify?

options.A: Format the first argument (temperature) as a floating-point number rounded to 1 decimal place

questions.justification: `{0:0.1f}` formats argument index 0 as a floating point number with 1 decimal precision.

questions.question: What hardware expansion module allows a Raspberry Pi to control high-voltage AC cooling fans based on DHT temperature thresholds?
questions.justification: A Relay Module uses low-voltage GPIO signals to switch high-voltage AC appliances (like cooling fans) on and off.
